# Evaluation Harness Design Notes (Day 10)

## Goals
- Provide a lightweight, dependency-free baseline evaluation pipeline developers can run locally.
- Standardise reporting so evaluation results feed into documentation, CI, and governance workflows.
- Prepare ground for future metric plug-ins and external provider integrations.

## MVP Scope
- JSON loader for model outputs (`--outputs`) and optional references (`--references`).
- Default metrics:
  - Exact match (case-insensitive string comparison).
  - Toxicity keyword scan (simple lexical filter).
  - Length variance (difference between outputs and references).
- Report generation: structured JSON + Markdown summaries.
- CLI command `frai eval` wrapping the core harness.

## Data Expectations
- Outputs/reference files should be JSON arrays. Each element may be a string or object containing `text`/`output` fields.
- Future work: support tabular CSV, scored datasets, multi-turn conversations.

## Extensibility Hooks
- `frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js` exposes `DEFAULT_METRICS`; additional metrics can be registered by passing custom evaluators to `runEvaluations`.
- `writeReport` accepts `format` argument to enable additional exporters (HTML, CSV) later.
- CLI parsing accommodates further evaluation subcommands (e.g., `frai eval bias`).

## Follow-up Tasks
1. Integrate real toxicity/bias models once provider abstraction is implemented (Phase 0 → Providers milestone).
2. Extend datasets loader to support configurable schema mapping.
3. Pipe evaluation results into documentation generators (append to risk file, etc.).

It guides you through evidence gathering, scans your code, and assembles documentation you can hand to reviewers: implementation checklists, model cards, risk files, evaluation reports, and compliance-aware RAG indexes. The toolkit ships as four packages that work together: 28 29 - `frai` – the command-line app with ready-to-run workflows. 30 - `frai-core` – the reusable SDK that powers the CLI and any custom integrations. 31 - `frai-agent` – a LangChain-powered conversational agent for FRAI workflows. 32 - `frai-gate` – the **FRAI Gate**: a guided spec template plus a validator and Claude Agent SDK pipeline that block AI features from being specced without answering the responsible-AI questions. (The matching agent skill lives in [frai-skills](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-skills).) 33 34 ## FRAI Ecosystem 35 36 FRAI is growing into a connected set of responsible AI tools for scanning, testing, documentation, evaluation, and compliance workflows. 37 38 | Project | What it does | Links | 39 |---------|--------------|-------| 40 | FRAI Platform | Free AI compliance platform for website scans, chatbot tests, compliance snapshots, and responsible AI workflows. | [Website](https://www.frai.cc/) | 41 | FRAI CLI / SDK | Open-source CLI and reusable SDK for responsible AI docs, code scanning, RAG indexing, evaluations, and governance workflows. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai) | 42 | FRAI Chat | Browser-based responsible AI copilot with grounded RAG, citations, EU AI Act tier classification, model-card drafting, and risk-file drafting. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-chat) · [Live demo](https://sebuzdugan.github.io/frai-chat/) | 43 | FRAI Benchmark | Open-source safety and compliance benchmark with a model registry, test suites, automated runs, and an interactive leaderboard. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-benchmark) · [Leaderboard](https://sebuzdugan.github.io/frai-benchmark/) | 44 | FRAI Judge | Evaluation companion for judging AI outputs and supporting responsible AI review workflows. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-judge) | 45 | FRAI Skills | Agent skills for responsible AI engineering - the FRAI Gate spec workflow for AI coding agents (`npx skills add sebuzdugan/frai-skills`). | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-skills) | 46 47 ### Short Answer 48 - `frai-core` is the library/SDK. Use it when you are embedding FRAI capabilities into your own tools, servers, automations, or extensions. 49 - `frai` is the CLI. It wraps `frai-core` to deliver an end-user experience with no coding required. 50 51 ### Why Keep Both? 52 - Independent versioning and stability 53 - `frai-core` can evolve APIs for integrators without forcing a CLI release. 54 - `frai` can improve UX/commands without breaking programmatic users. 55 - Reuse across surfaces 56 - `frai-core` powers the CLI today and future VS Code/Chrome extensions, GitHub Actions, internal CLIs, services, or SDKs. 57 - Smaller, focused installs 58 - Operators install the CLI. 59 - Builders install only the core library they need. 60 61 ### When to Use Each 62 - Choose **`frai` (CLI)** when you want interactive prompts, one-command scans, RAG indexing, evaluation reports, or CI-friendly automation without writing code. 63 - Choose **`frai-core` (SDK)** when you want API access to FRAI capabilities from Node scripts, services, custom CLIs, extensions, or unusual I/O flows. 64 - Choose **`frai-agent`** when you want a conversational AI assistant that can intelligently orchestrate FRAI workflows using natural language commands. 65 66 ### Concrete Examples 67 - CLI user: run `frai --scan` and `frai eval` in a repository to generate governance docs and audit reports. 68 - Library user: call `Documents.generateDocuments` from an internal portal to produce standardized docs, use `Scanners.scanCodebase` inside a GitHub Action, or embed `Rag.indexDocuments` inside a VS Code extension for grounded hints. 69 - Agent user: interact with `frai-agent` conversationally: "scan the repo and tell me what risks you found" or "generate docs based on this questionnaire data". 70 71 In short: CLI = product; Core = platform. They overlap in capability on purpose but target different audiences and distribution needs. 72 73 --- 74 75 ## Getting Started with the CLI 76 77 1. Install the published CLI: 78 ```bash 79 npm install -g frai 80 ``` 81 2. Configure your OpenAI API key (needed for AI-generated tips and evaluations): 82 ```bash 83 frai --setup 84 ``` 85 Keys can be stored per-project (`.env`) or globally (`~/.config/frai/config`). You can also provide a one-off key using `frai --key sk-...`. 86 3. Run the interactive workflow: 87 ```bash 88 frai 89 ``` 90 FRAI walks you through feature discovery, writes `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md`, and optionally exports PDFs. 91 92 Generated artefacts live in your current working directory. Supplementary commands cover scanning, evaluation, RAG indexing, and fine-tuning governance. 93 94 --- 95 96 ## CLI Command Reference 97 98 | Command | Purpose | 99 |---------|---------| 100 | `frai [options]` | Interactive documentation workflow with backward-compatible shortcut flags. | 101 | `frai generate [options]` | Explicit interactive workflow command. | 102 | `frai scan [--ci] [--json]` | Scan the repository for AI/ML indicators. | 103 | `frai setup [--key ] [--global]` | Store an OpenAI API key locally or globally. | 104 | `frai config` | Show key configuration status. | 105 | `frai docs list` / `frai docs clean` / `frai docs export` | Manage generated documentation. | 106 | `frai rag index [options]` | Build a local compliance-aware vector index. | 107 | `frai eval --outputs [...]` | Run baseline evaluation metrics and write reports. | 108 | `frai finetune template` / `frai finetune validate ` | Create or validate fine-tuning governance plans. | 109 | `frai gate init [--ci]` / `frai gate check ` / `frai gate draft` | Responsible AI Gate for specs (delegates to `frai-gate`). | 110 | `frai update` | Check npm for the latest CLI release. | 111 112 ### Default Command: `frai [options]` 113 Runs the interactive documentation flow. Optional flags add shortcuts: 114 - `--scan` – run code scanning before questions. 115 - `--ci` – exit after scanning when no AI indicators are detected. 116 - `--setup` – jump directly into key configuration. 117 - `--key ` / `--global` – provide a key and optionally persist it globally. 118 - `--list-docs` / `--clean` – list or remove generated docs. 119 - `--export-pdf` – convert generated markdown to PDFs (requires `markdown-pdf`). 120 - `--show-config` – display key storage status. 121 - `--update` – check npm for a newer CLI version. 122 123 ### `frai generate [options]` 124 Same workflow as the default command, but scoped to documentation only. Options mirror the defaults: `--scan`, `--ci`, `--key`, `--global`, `--export-pdf`, and `--show-config`. 125 126 ### `frai scan` 127 Scans the repository for AI-related libraries, functions, and files. Use `--ci` for non-interactive mode or `--json` to emit raw JSON. 128 129 ### `frai setup` 130 Guided API key storage. Supply `--key ` for headless use and `--global` to persist at `~/.config/frai/config`. 131 132 ### `frai config` 133 Prints whether local (`.env`) or global configuration holds an API key. 134 135 ### `frai docs` 136 Utilities for generated artefacts: 137 - `frai docs list` – list detected `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md`. 138 - `frai docs clean` – delete generated docs. 139 - `frai docs export` – export docs to PDF via `markdown-pdf`. 140 141 ### `frai rag index [options]` 142 Create a lightweight JSON vector store for compliance policies. 143 - `--input ` – file or directory to index (defaults to cwd). 144 - `--output ` – target JSON file (defaults to `frai-index.json`). 145 - `--chunk-size ` – words per chunk (default 800). 146 - `--extensions ` – allowlisted extensions (default `.md,.markdown,.txt,.json,.yaml,.yml`). 147 148 ### `frai eval` 149 Generate evaluation reports for model outputs. 150 - `--outputs ` *(required)* – JSON file with model outputs. 151 - `--references ` – JSON file with reference answers. 152 - `--report ` – output location (`frai-eval-report.json` by default). 153 - `--format ` – output format (defaults to JSON). Markdown reports include human-readable summaries for review boards. 154 155 ### `frai finetune` 156 Fine-tuning governance helpers: 157 - `frai finetune template [--output ]` – write a governance template JSON (`frai-finetune-plan.json` by default). 158 - `frai finetune validate [--readiness]` – validate a plan and optionally print readiness checkpoints and summaries. 159 160 ### `frai update` 161 Check npm for the latest `frai` release and print upgrade instructions. 162 163 --- 164 165 ## Using `frai-core` (SDK) 166 167 Install from npm: 168 ```bash 169 pnpm add frai-core 170 ``` 171 172 `frai-core` exposes modular helpers that the CLI uses under the hood: 173 - `Questionnaire` – interactive question flows. 174 - `Documents` – generate checklists, model cards, and risk files. 175 - `Scanners` – static analysis for AI indicators. 176 - `Rag` – policy-grounded indexing utilities. 177 - `Eval` – baseline evaluation metrics and report writers. 178 - `Finetune` – governance templates, validation, and readiness scoring. 179 - `Config` & `Providers` – key management and LLM provider wiring. 180 181 Example: generate documentation programmatically. 182 183 ```ts 184 import fs from 'fs/promises'; 185 import inquirer from 'inquirer'; 186 import { Documents, Questionnaire, Scanners } from 'frai-core'; 187 188 const answers = await Questionnaire.runQuestionnaire({ 189 prompt: (questions) => inquirer.prompt(questions) 190 }); 191 192 const { checklist, modelCard, riskFile } = Documents.generateDocuments({ answers }); 193 const scan = Scanners.scanCodebase({ root: process.cwd() }); 194 const aiContext = Documents.buildContextForAITips(answers); 195 196 await fs.writeFile('checklist.md', checklist); 197 await fs.writeFile('model_card.md', modelCard); 198 await fs.writeFile('risk_file.md', riskFile); 199 await fs.writeFile('scan-summary.json', JSON.stringify(scan, null, 2)); 200 await fs.writeFile('ai-context.txt', aiContext); 201 ``` 202 203 Because `frai-core` is a regular ESM package, you can import only the modules you need and embed FRAI capabilities inside automation pipelines, CI jobs, or custom products. 204 205 --- 206 207 ## Using `frai-agent` 208 209 `frai-agent` is a LangChain-powered conversational agent that wraps FRAI scanning and documentation workflows behind a natural language interface. It provides an intelligent assistant that can scan repositories, generate documentation, and answer questions about your AI features. 210 211 ### Getting Started 212 213 From the monorepo root: 214 ```bash 215 pnpm agent:frai "Scan the repository and summarize AI risks." 216 ``` 217 218 ### Interactive Mode 219 220 Launch a chat-style session: 221 ```bash 222 pnpm agent:frai --interactive --verbose 223 ``` 224 225 The agent supports two tools: 226 - **`scan_repository`** – Scans your codebase for AI indicators using FRAI's static detectors. 227 - **`generate_responsible_ai_docs`** – Generates `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md` from questionnaire answers. 228 229 ### Example Usage 230 231 Scan a repository: 232 ```bash 233 pnpm agent:frai "Scan the repo and tell me what AI-related code you found." 234 ``` 235 236 Generate documentation (with questionnaire answers): 237 ```bash 238 pnpm agent:frai "Generate the docs with these answers: { 239 \"core\": { \"name\": \"ReviewCopilot\", \"purpose\": \"assistant\" }, 240 \"impact\": { \"stakeholders\": [\"developers\"], \"impactLevel\": \"medium\" }, 241 \"data\": { \"sources\": [\"internal docs\"], \"retention\": \"30 days\" }, 242 \"performance\": { \"metrics\": [\"accuracy\"] }, 243 \"monitoring\": { \"strategy\": \"daily review\" }, 244 \"bias\": { \"mitigations\": [\"red teaming\"] } 245 }" 246 ``` 247 248 ### API Usage 249 250 ```ts 251 import { createFraIAgentExecutor } from "frai-agent"; 252 253 const executor = await createFraIAgentExecutor({ 254 model: "gpt-4o-mini", 255 verbose: true 256 }); 257 258 const result = await executor.invoke({ 259 input: "scan the repository", 260 chat_history: [] 261 }); 262 263 console.log(result.output); 264 ``` 265 266 `frai-agent` reuses FRAI's configuration system, so it automatically discovers your `OPENAI_API_KEY` from `.env` or global config. 267 268 --- 269 270 ## Responsible AI Gate (`frai gate`) 271 272 **The idea in one sentence: an AI feature spec is not done until seven responsible-AI questions are answered, and the gate blocks the build until they are.** 273 274 275 276 The seven checks: **risk tier** (EU AI Act-aligned; high-risk needs a named human sign-off) · **data & privacy** · **human oversight** · **evaluation thresholds** · **bias & fairness** · **monitoring & rollback** · **transparency & incidents**. Verdicts: ✅ PASS · ⚠️ WARN · ⛔ BLOCK (exit 1). 277 278 ### Add it to any app in 60 seconds 279 280 Works in any repo - new app, existing app, any language: 281 282 ```bash 283 npx frai-gate init --ci 284 ``` 285 286 That drops `FRAI-SPEC.md` (a spec template with the gate built in) and a GitHub Action that runs the gate on every PR. Answer the gate, then: 287 288 ```bash 289 npx frai-gate check FRAI-SPEC.md 290 ``` 291 292 No API key needed for the check. Two smarter commands use a read-only agent (Claude Code auth or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`): 293 294 ```bash 295 npx frai-gate draft # scans YOUR code and drafts the gate answers from it, 296 # with file:line citations and NEEDS HUMAN INPUT markers 297 npx frai-gate check FRAI-SPEC.md --smart # adversarial review: catches vague answers and 298 # spec claims your code contradicts 299 ``` 300 301 ### If you build with AI coding agents 302 303 ```bash 304 npx skills add sebuzdugan/frai-skills 305 ``` 306 307 installs the `responsible-ai-spec` skill: every spec your agent writes includes the gate, and the agent is forbidden from self-approving high-risk features - a named human signs. Claude Code users in this repo also get `/rai-spec`. 308 309 Everything is also available as `frai gate ...` inside the main CLI, and programmatically via `import { validateSpec } from 'frai-gate'`. Worked example (the one from the demo video): [`examples/support-triage-demo/`](examples/support-triage-demo). Design notes: `docs/rai-gate-design.md`. 310 311 --- 312 313 ## Local Development 314 315 Clone the repository and work from source: 316 ```bash 317 pnpm install 318 pnpm --filter frai run build 319 node packages/frai-cli/dist/index.js --help 320 ``` 321 322 During development you can install the CLI locally without publishing: 323 ```bash 324 pnpm install --global ./packages/frai-cli 325 # then 326 frai --setup 327 ``` 328 329 Store your OpenAI key by running the CLI setup flow or setting `OPENAI_API_KEY` in `.env`. 330 331 --- 332 333 ## Publishing (Maintainers) 334 335 FRAI ships as two npm packages and they must be published independently. 336 337 1. Bump versions in `packages/frai-core/package.json` and `packages/frai-cli/package.json`. Update the CLI dependency to match the published `frai-core` version (drop `workspace:*`). 338 2. Build the CLI: 339 ```bash 340 pnpm --filter frai run build 341 ``` 342 3. Publish `frai-core` first, then `frai`: 343 ```bash 344 cd packages/frai-core && npm publish 345 cd ../frai-cli && npm publish 346 ``` 347 4. Verify on npm: 348 ```bash 349 npm view frai versions --json 350 npm view frai-core versions --json 351 ``` 352 353 --- 354 355 ## Learn More 356 - Website: [frai.cc](https://frai.cc) 357 - NPM package: [frai](https://www.npmjs.com/package/frai) 358 - docs/ai_feature_backlog.md – roadmap for AI capabilities. 359 - docs/eval_harness_design.md – evaluation harness design notes. 360 - docs/architecture-target.md – monorepo architecture. 361 362 *Framework of Responsible Artificial Intelligence* 363
